claims.text: The initial homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The interfaces in the initial lamellar structure are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but is brittle.
Stress concentration at incoherent interfaces causes the brittleness of the initial alloy.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the dual-phase lamellae into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructure will possess coherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces will facilitate dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces will alleviate interfacial stress concentrations.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure will enable dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
The enabled deformation mechanisms will distribute strain homogeneously.
Homogeneous strain distribution will arrest interfacial cracking.
The HPHT-induced microstructure will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The treated sample will exhibit elongated cracks rather than isolated microcracks on its fracture surface.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
Convergence of the phase-specific GND densities indicates homogeneous strain distribution.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce the same hierarchical interface coherence or GND homogenization.
Pressure and temperature must be high enough to induce the lamellar-to-hierarchical transformation but low enough to avoid phase instability.
The proposed effect is specific to the topological transformation produced under the stated HPHT conditions.
